The booklet pictures are small, so I guessed several placements and rests_on links. Treat them as approximate. This applies especially to the grate slopes, the 4287b inverted slopes, the 12825 clip tiles, the 1x2 plates and the fin and canopy pieces.

The pieces were added in this order. Step 1: 4x4 plate. Step 2: two grates. Step 3: yellow 2x6. Step 4: two wheel holders. Step 5: 1x2 plate. Step 6: grey 2x6. Step 7: the front sub-assembly of 1x4 plate, two trans-yellow tiles and curved brick. Step 8: two red round plates after flipping the model. Step 9: wheel arches and clip tiles. Step 10: 1x2 plate and two flames. Step 11: studded arch, corner plates and inverted slopes. Step 12: grey 2x2 plate, grates and a 1x2 plate. Step 13: mudguard, 1x6 tiles and canopy. Step 14: wheels and tyres.
The clip tiles are assumed to clip onto the wheel holders. The wheels are assumed to sit on the wheel-holder axles, and each tyre is assumed to be on its wheel.
The 3022 plate in step 12 is assumed to be the base for the windscreen cheese slopes and tiles, and the 1x2 plates are assumed to be small fillers.

Step 1: b1 and b2 are two black 4x10 plates side by side. Tiles b3 and b4 cross both plates at the ends. b5 (printed tile) is on the front plate and b6 on the back plate.

Step 3-4: Each 4x6 plate (b7, b8) spans both base plates. The four 1x6 tiles are in a pinwheel on the 4x6 plates. I could not read exactly which plate each tile covers, so all four list both b7 and b8.
The 2x2 tiles b16-b19 and the stacked round plates b13/b14 are listed as resting on b7 and b8. This is a guess from the page 6 picture.
Hub-and-connector sub-assemblies (b21 with b22-b24, and b42 with b43-b45) are single steps. The lower connectors sit with their pin holes over the dish studs, so I listed them as resting on b20.

Step 9: each red axle (b29, b31, b33, b35) goes into the connector below it and the connector above it. I could not tell this for certain from the pictures. The top red axle b35 goes into b36 in step 10.
Step 12: the bush b40 is shown but its exact spot is unclear. I placed it on top of connector b39 on axle b41. The hub b42 then rests on it.
Hoses b46-b48 are not cut in the model. The scissors mark on page 12 is a guide only. Each hose joins one lower connector to one upper connector.
Step 18: round plate b53 is pushed into the underside of dish b52 and rests on b50. The dish b52 rests on the 40-tooth gear b51 and on b53.

Step 19: dish b54 (4x4), round plate b55 (1x1), dish b56 (2x2) and antenna b57 are stacked and then placed on dish b52. In the real set the booklet element codes differ from the catalogue ids, so I used the catalogue ids from the parts list.

The booklet genuinely builds TWO separate models: Naida's gondola (steps 1-13, pieces b1-b31) and the goblin's rock hideout (its own steps 1-15, pieces b32-b63). Each restarts step numbering, and page 30 shows them as two free-standing models side by side. They share no connection, so the two groups are kept separate on purpose.
The goblin (b62) stands on the green curved brick b38 so the figure and his card are part of the hideout model.
The second lime flower with purple round plate (b59/b61) sits on a stud of the base plate b32 (page 15 shows it dropped at the front of the base), not on the stud-less round tile b43.
Naida's mini-doll pieces (hair, head, torso, legs) are not in the official parts list, so they are omitted. Her bowl (b31, lego-98138) is linked loosely to the bottle head as an assumption.
Positions inside the hulls, wedge plates and plates are approximated from the isometric booklet views; rests_on lists are best-effort.
lego-6266 'Leg Skeleton' is the light-grey skeleton seen on step 8 of the goblin scene (booklet element 6038453).
Gem 24 facet counts: 2 Trans-Bright Green in the basket, 1 Trans-Clear as the telescope lens. Totals match the 63-piece list.
The booklet drawings are small and ambiguous, so the exact position of some pieces is my best reading. All 53 pieces and each part type's count match the parts list.

Reading of the build: a 2x4 plate and a 2x2 plate sit on the lime base between two black 1x2 plates. A 1x4 brick and a 1x2 brick go on the back, black curved legs on the sides, and two black curved 2x1 pieces on the front 2x2 plate. Two red side-stud bricks form the chest, with black 1x1 plates and inverted brackets at each side.

The 6091 arms sit on the bracket and the 1x1 black plate. A black 2x2x2/3 plate and black 2x2 plate carry four 1x1 side-stud bricks for the head. A white 2x2 plate, two jumper plates and the dark pink 1x2 plate cap the head.
Step 15 shows a black piece pushed onto the head from the side; I treated it as the black round nose tile on a head side stud.
Ears are white clip plates pushed sideways onto side studs, each with a black round tile on its stud. Eyes are the printed tiles on front side studs.

The foot is a white 2x2 plate on the two side studs of the 99206, with a jumper plate, a curved 15068 and a black round tile. Three more white 1x2 plate + curved 15068 sub-assemblies (the '3x' box) are pushed onto head side studs.
The heart goes onto the front red brick's side studs in step 18.

Two black 6091 curved bricks (b52, b53) are placed on the pink head plate and on the heart studs. This is an assumption made to account for the parts list, because the booklet is unclear about the last two 6091.
The 15068 element is listed as 6552147 in the inventory but appears as 6047220 in the booklet; I used the inventory type.
All connections are modelled as rests_on or other_joins. Positions are left null.
The minifigure (head, hair, torso, legs) on pages 2 and 15 is not in the 62-piece parts list, so it is not recorded.

The booklet builds the car and then, in step 13, the doctor's hand-held gauge/handle accessory (b58-b60). The briefcase b61 is a loose prop. Neither is fastened to the car. To keep one connected graph I added two loose joins (b58-b61 and b58-b42). These are assumptions, not connections shown in the booklet.

Frame: x runs left to right, y runs front (y=0, face side) to back (y=3). The body's base plate b1 is the belt, so the figure is built upright.

Step 3: the 4 dark blue 1x1 plates are stacked two high at each end of the brown 1x4 plate. The clip plate b9 and the plain 1x2 plate b10 are stacked in the middle. The finished unit sits on the back dark blue brick b2.
Step 4: the two yellow round bricks fill the 2x2 hole in the middle of the 4x4 base.

Step 8: the first ring of six grey bracket bricks has two bricks on each side (left and right) and one in the middle of the front and back. Step 10: the second ring is the opposite, with two bricks on the front and back and one in the middle of each side. This matches the head views and the side-stud faces the later plates and tiles attach to. The ring sits on the brown plates.
Pieces that attach to horizontal (side) studs of the grey bracket bricks are recorded in other_joins with rests_on empty. This covers the head front, ears, back, and the arm sub-assemblies.
In steps 6 and 7 the tile and clip plate rest on the 2x2 plate (built flat), and that plate is then attached sideways to the grey bracket brick on that side.

Step 12-13 face: the two 2x3 plates cover three stud rows. The tan 1x4 plate takes the bottom row and the tan tile covers it. The dark blue 1x4 plate with two studs takes the next row, and the A tile covers the top two rows. The eyes sit on the two studs of that plate.

Steps 15-18: each ear fills a 4x2 block of side studs on the lower bracket bricks. Each side has a dark tan 1x2 tile and a dark blue 1x2 tile, a dark tan and a dark blue 1x1 tile, and a vertical tan 1x2 plate. The tan slope sits on that plate, and a 2x4 dark blue tile covers the upper bracket brick. The left side is a mirror of the right.

Step 21: the 2x2 plate is attached with its studs up into the underside of the base plate b1 (model turned over). In the upright figure it hangs below b1. Step 22: each leg is a dark blue 1x2 brick on a black 1x2 plate (foot), and the leg brick fits into the underside of the 2x2 plate.
The shield clips onto the left (viewer's left) hand clip b27, as in the final picture. Clip-to-shield is recorded as a clip join, but the exact grip detail is assumed.

Step 23: the base is a black 4x6 plate with the nameplate tile on it. The black 2-stud plate and the black 1x4 tile are placed on the base. The feet b72 and b74 are placed on the base studs. The exact base layout is partly assumed from the small illustration.
Piece counts match the parts list: 79 pieces.

The booklet is a low-resolution 3D drawing set and several steps (3-7 plates, 8-12 ring plates, 17-18 roof) are ambiguous. Exact stacking is my best reading; the type, colour and count of every piece matches the parts list (74 pieces).
Plates that are clipped to the underside of the 12-long bricks (b4, b5, b58) are recorded with rests_on pointing to the bricks they clutch, since they clutch pieces rather than sit on them.

KEPT AS TWO GROUPS ON PURPOSE: the shovel (b74, lego-3837) is the only piece not joined to the tractor. The booklet shows it only as the minifigure's hand-held tool (page 3 and step 21). The minifigure itself is not in the parts list, so there is nothing for the shovel to be held by. The booklet shows no step that attaches the shovel to the tractor, so any join would be invented. The other 73 pieces form one connected tractor. This is a real separate item, not a missed connection.
The sticker sheet is a single part (b45); the wheat sticker is on the red brick at step 14 and the second sticker (grille) at step 21 comes from the same sheet.
Steps 4-5: both friction pins and the yellow bar are placed by the end pin holes at the rear; the bar passes through the pins.

The tipper (steps on page 16) is built as a sub-assembly: 2x2 plate with pin holes, two blue axle pins, two pole reverser handles, and the tipper bed on top. It is attached at step 19 by the reverser axles going into the axle holes of the two angled connectors (b13, b14).
Step 20: one 7L axle passes through both rear wheels and the pin holes of the two 1x2 Technic bricks. The front wheels go on the pins of the wheel holder plate (b58).
Red 1x6 plates (b33, b34) are placed under the wheel arches (b43, b44) as the wheel arch is mounted on a plate row.
Total 91 pieces, matching the parts list. The sticker sheet (b29) is one piece used three times: bumper, hood and roof.

The remaining 3 groups are real, so I kept them. (1) The truck, steps 1-26 on pages 4-28. (2) The street lamp with traffic light, a second model with its own steps 1-5 on pages 29-33. The booklet never attaches it to the truck. (3) The wrench b91, which the minifigure holds in its hands and which attaches to nothing.
The minifigure (hard hat, head, torso, legs) is on page 2 but is not in the parts list, so it is not recorded. The wrench is the only listed part that belongs to it.
The jumper plate b49 rests on the orange rear plate b3, because the tile b47 has no studs.
The traffic-light brick b82 is slid onto the bar of the flag-pole tile b81 (other_join), because the tile has no studs.

Base steps 1-3 are built upside down. The black 2x3 plate (b2) and orange 2x4 plate (b3) are under the base ends, and the wheel holders (b4, b5) are under those plates. So b1 rests on b2 and b3, b2 rests on b4, and b3 rests on b5.
The exact stud footprints of the cab pieces (b31-b43), the rear slopes and the front assembly are inferred from the small isometric drawings, so some rests_on lists may be incomplete.
b87 rests on b89 because the yellow plate is attached under the hinge plate. Its id is later than b87 because of build order.
Doors b37 and b38 hang on the clips b32 and b31 and have no stud contact. The hammer (b79) is assumed to be held in clip b31.
The cones (b67, b68) and round tiles (b69, b70) are treated as resting on the piece below. Side-attached traffic-light lenses (b83, b84) are other_joins.

Remaining 'two groups' finding is NOT a real problem and is intentionally kept: the sheep, its base and every other brick form ONE connected model (head joined to body, 4 legs pinned to the body, feet resting on green plate b83). The only other group is the Year Of The Sheep envelope (b100, lego-6116050), a paper insert listed in the official inventory that the booklet never attaches to the model. It must stay in the list to match the parts count, and inventing a connection to it would be false.
Booklet drawings are small; exact stud-level resting relationships for several pieces (body plates, head steps 3-6, base layers 4-8, rock pieces) are best-effort inferences.
Base: the 2nd brown 4x6 plate (b68) is slid under the overhanging end of the blue 2x4 brick (b67), so b67 rests on b63 and b68.
Legs: each built as 15672 -> 3024 -> 3005 -> 3665 -> 3700 -> 85984; steps 12 (2x) and 13 (2x). Pins b7,b8 face the near side for legs of step 12; b12,b13 face the far side for legs of step 13.
Final assembly (page 27): sheep feet rest on green 2x6 plate b83; an assumption, since the booklet shows no numbered step for it.
Pins b7,b8,b12,b13 have empty rests_on because they are side-inserted pins.
Totals match the 105-piece parts list. The minifigure parts (head, torso, legs, helmet, orange armour, trans-green stud) are not in the parts list, so they are not recorded.
Several rests_on lists are best guesses. The booklet art is low-resolution, and in some steps (body steps 4-6, the head brackets, the paw layers) I could not tell which pieces sit on which.

Body: the dark towball plates are shown as sitting on the 2x6 plate. The 4 side balls (b7, b8, b11, b12) are assigned as: b11 and b12 take the rear legs A and B, b7 and b8 take the front legs C and D, and b15 on top of the front pair takes the head.

Part-number mapping: 2540 is the white side-handle plate (body step 5, head step 2). 4081b is the white clip plate in head step 6. 50950 is the curved 3x1 in the front-leg step 6, and 85984 is the pair of ear slopes. 11477 is used twice in the rear legs and twice on the head cheeks.

Leg A is the rear-right leg (booklet step 9), leg B is the rear-left (step 10), leg C is the front-near leg (step 11) and leg D is the front-far leg (step 12). The four paws (step 13, 4x) are each joined to a leg by ball and socket.
The booklet shows two tooth plates (49668) per front leg. I put one on top of the 14704 and one under it, clutching its underside, so the lower one has an empty rests_on and an other_join.

Connectivity fix: the build was split into four groups, which the booklet does not mean. The beast, the sword with its hand piece, the shield and the loose card were not linked. The minifigure rides on the beast's back (page 31) but is not in the parts list, so its pieces are not recorded. I let the pearl-gold hand piece (b102) stand in for the minifigure and rest on a body plate (b9). The sword and shield are joined to that hand piece.

The sticker sheet is joined to the head print piece as a representative join, since the stickers go on the head, legs and paws. The trading card is a loose paper item. I linked it to the sticker sheet by a non-fastened contact only so it is not an orphan; it is not really built into the model.
All 104 pieces of the parts list are included, with each type appearing exactly the listed number of times.
The pilot minifigure (page 2/26) is not in the parts list, so it is not recorded.

The booklet pictures leave several exact stud positions ambiguous: which stack each wing wedge sits on, the black plates around the cockpit, the tail cap and wing struts, and which clips take the tools. Those rests_on entries are best guesses.
Each of the four 6141 stack positions is assumed to be 2 plates high on the black 3020, since the 8 plates are shown as stacked pairs.
The upper wing is built on its own (page 20) and then lowered onto the two struts in step 24. Its rests_on therefore lists the struts.
The undercarriage plate with pins (30157) is clutched under the black plate holding the round-plate stacks and is recorded as a join, not a rest.
Pieces with no stud connection to the model (axle, bushes, tools, propeller, cowl and similar) have an empty rests_on and are recorded in other_joins.
